body:
Yes, I think I can see what's happening...

1. `Initialize` is called with level `Off`.
2. `Tracewriter` is left null but `Initialized` is set to true.
3. `Initialize` is called a second time, with any level specified.
4. The else clause is executed with a null `TraceWriter`.

So we changed to allow re-initialization at a different level while the framework is still trying to protect itself against re-initialization. This didn't show up as a problem until we implemented the further change of lazily creating the `TraceWriter`.

We can't do both things... lazy creation and using the null value as an indicator of creation.

Nice find!
Based on the existing code, I assume the desired behavior here is that this can be called multiple times, and the internal tracer should only be created the first time a level other that "Off" is specified?

In other words, the level can be changed from "Off" -> "something", but not from "something" -> "Off"?

No, initialization should only be called once and the data provided saved. If the level is changed on the fly, it is done by setting the property. The file should be created either on first write or when the level is set to something other than off. I have wrote code for this for this which may only be in the engine's copy of InternalTrace - I'll have to check.

So as a minimum the code should be changed like:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/203432/202487521-4f5d1b7f-0a11-4549-ab6b-913f0f6c813f.png)
It has to be done in both methods though.

But, the Initialized property is only stating that the traceWriter is null or not, so why are they independent?  That's the underlying reason for this crash.   If the property is needed (which I assume it is), why not let it just be like:
```cs
 public static bool Initialized  => traceWriter != null;
```
Would be less code to write too.

I feel like it's somewhat more complicated than just that fix. I feel I should look into this a bit more deeply and make some suggestions to the framework team... maybe even a PR. I have a few other things to fix first. :-)

But the framework code, though flawed, is intended to avoid multiple calls to `InternalTrace.Initialize`. That seems to be the heart of the matter. How is the adapter directly or indirectly calling this more than once for the same assembly?

UPDATE - I see this __is__ a framework issue now. Apparently transfered. Very confusing. :-)

I raised this issue here in the NUnit repo, it has never been elsewhere.  And did so because the stack trace pointed to this method.

The underlying reason for calling it multiple times comes from how the tests are run inside the adapter test project.  It uses the adapter code at the same time as it tests it.  It has been like this for ~8 years now, so it must be the latest change we did there to set the InternalTraceLevel for the engine that triggers this.  But the change I have suggested here is doing the same as before, just in a more safe manner.

Awesome if you can have a deeper look and see if there is something more to this.  But the code should not be as it was in any case.

My mistake then. I saw your name and made that assumption. My comments have therefore been aimed at the adapter not the framework up to now. Possibly confusing to everyone I guess.

I disagree that your statement that the change you propose does the same as before.

Original behavior: Log an error if `InitializeTrace` is called more than once.
New behavior: Log an error if `InitializeTrace` is called more than once unless all earlier calls used a level of `Off`.

Of course it's up to @rprouse and the @nunit/framework-team to decide which behavior they want.

If they want the original behavior then simply using `traceWriter?.WriteLine` would prevent the error. That, however, leads to the question "How will the caller ever learn that the call was invalid.?" Maybe I should have just thrown an exception in the first place. :-)

(I acknowledge of course that throwing would be a breaking change, so we can't do it now.)

I agree the change does change the behavior as you state there.  

Protecting the call to Writeline is an option, but why is it that the call can't be set to Off first (like we do in the adapter for the engine (I have not checked if that call is propagated down here) and then set for each package (I assume that those calls are the ones that are actually propagated down here).  Using Off first makes it possible to first set it as a default value, then a bit later set it to the actually wanted level.  When looking from the adapter's "point of view" that makes more sense to me, but then I  am ignoring other possible ways this would be used, unknown to me.

On the other hand, this might be an "adapter test only" issue.  And the tests in question comes from way back.  @jnm2 added acceptance tests to the adapter a while back, and those are isolated, and running in their own process. All of those are working.  These tests (loading and using the Mockassembly) are kind of early versions of that, and should possibly be run in isolation too. I don't think the adapter is able to run anything else in this manner though. 
The code should be fixed anyway since it is not robust, but either of the ways would work. 

Btw, throwing an exception would effectively stop any way of that kind of testing.

And, I am currently trying to release the 4.3.1 hotfix, but I do have a bunch of failing tests.  I suspect that they are caused by this, but I haven't gone through them all. I am reluctant to release anything with failing tests. 

UPDATE:
I can release a beta though, but a beta for a hotfix feels a bit off.

I think your adapter tests are proof that the original concept (mine btw) of ignoring and logging subsequent initialization was a mistake. If an error had been thrown eight years ago, you would have tested in a more isolated way. I think both I and others were more casual about ignoring errors than we like to be today. Of course, the point of the log is that you should know about this problem because something may change in the future... as it now has.

The basic problem is that the `Initialize` method sets up two things: the file to which writing will be done and the trace level. In  the change that led to the "empty file error" the intent was that the level might change, but not the file. In principal, the caller has no way to know whether that file has been written to. So really, an entire (breaking) restructuring of what trace does would be the cleanest approach. All of what we are seeing here is really an attempt to do the same thing without breaking anything.

In agree that your change would be the most expedient and it does bring the framework `InternalTrace` closer to the other copies. I'm thinking that we should eventually review each copy for consistency. (I can't quite remember how many there are, but more than one for sure)

issue.title: TestOutputXml regressions

milestone.description: Hotfix for #1027, #1026 and regression fix for #987

repository.name: nunit3-vs-adapter
repository.description: NUnit 3.0 Visual Studio test adapter for use under VS 2012 or later

issue.body:
Our current setup is
```
<PackageReference Include="Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk" Version="17.2.0" />
<PackageReference Include="NUnit3TestAdapter" Version="4.2.1" />
```

Using .NET Core 6.0.100.

We use a settings like that looks like
```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<RunSettings>
  <NUnit>
  <DiscoveryMethod>Legacy</DiscoveryMethod>
  <DisplayName>FullName</DisplayName>
    <Where>test == 'BuildPerformance.Tests.Windows.AveragedBuildPerformanceTests.DotsSample'</Where>
    <TestOutputXml>C:/UnitySrc/dev/il2cpp-7/results/TestResult_NUnitTest</TestOutputXml>
  </NUnit>
</RunSettings>
```

And the `dotnet test` command looks like
```
dotnet test C:\UnitySrc\dev\il2cpp-7\il2cpp.sln -p:SolutionDir="C:\UnitySrc\dev\il2cpp-7/" --no-build --no-restore --nologo --configuration Debug --settings "C:\UnitySrc\dev\il2cpp-7\results\RunSettings_NUnitTest.xml"
```

All Good. 

I'm updating to net7 and have updated to the 7.0.100 sdk.  Updated my packages
```
<PackageReference Include="Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk" Version="17.4.0" />
<PackageReference Include="NUnit3TestAdapter" Version="4.3.0" />
```

Everything else is the same.

Boom.
```
System.ArgumentNullException: Value cannot be null. (Parameter 'path1')
   at System.ArgumentNullException.Throw(String paramName)
   at System.IO.Path.Combine(String path1, String path2)
   at NUnit.VisualStudio.TestAdapter.AdapterSettings.SetTestOutputFolder() in D:\repos\NUnit\nunit3-vs-adapter\src\NUnitTestAdapter\AdapterSettings.cs:line 434
   at NUnit.VisualStudio.TestAdapter.AdapterSettings.Load(String settingsXml) in D:\repos\NUnit\nunit3-vs-adapter\src\NUnitTestAdapter\AdapterSettings.cs:line 345
   at NUnit.VisualStudio.TestAdapter.AdapterSettings.Load(IDiscoveryContext context) in D:\repos\NUnit\nunit3-vs-adapter\src\NUnitTestAdapter\AdapterSettings.cs:line 311
   at NUnit.VisualStudio.TestAdapter.NUnitTestAdapter.Initialize(IDiscoveryContext context, IMessageLogger messageLogger) in D:\repos\NUnit\nunit3-vs-adapter\src\NUnitTestAdapter\NUnitTestAdapter.cs:line 135
Exception System.ArgumentException,    Exception thrown executing tests in C:\UnitySrc\dev\il2cpp-s-1\il2cpp-s-1\Unity.IL2CPP.Debugger.Soft.Tests\bin\Debug\net7.0\Unity.IL2CPP.Debugger.Soft.Tests.dll
The value cannot be an empty string. (Parameter 'path')
   at System.ArgumentException.ThrowNullOrEmptyException(String argument, String paramName)
   at System.IO.Directory.CreateDirectory(String path)
   at NUnit.VisualStudio.TestAdapter.NUnit3TestExecutor.CreateTestOutputFolder() in D:\repos\NUnit\nunit3-vs-adapter\src\NUnitTestAdapter\NUnit3TestExecutor.cs:line 365
   at NUnit.VisualStudio.TestAdapter.NUnit3TestExecutor.RunAssembly(String assemblyPath, IGrouping`2 testCases, TestFilter filter) in D:\repos\NUnit\nunit3-vs-adapter\src\NUnitTestAdapter\NUnit3TestExecutor.cs:line 275

```

I started poking around and found `OutputXmlFolderMode`.  I added the following to our settings file
```
<OutputXmlFolderMode>AsSpecified</OutputXmlFolderMode>
```

Boom.
```
Exception System.ArgumentException,    Exception thrown executing tests in C:\UnitySrc\dev\il2cpp-s-1\il2cpp-s-1\Unity.IL2CPP.Debugger.Soft.Tests\bin\Debug\net7.0\Unity.IL2CPP.Debugger.Soft.Tests.dll
The value cannot be an empty string. (Parameter 'path')
   at System.ArgumentException.ThrowNullOrEmptyException(String argument, String paramName)
   at System.IO.Directory.CreateDirectory(String path)
   at NUnit.VisualStudio.TestAdapter.NUnit3TestExecutor.CreateTestOutputFolder() in D:\repos\NUnit\nunit3-vs-adapter\src\NUnitTestAdapter\NUnit3TestExecutor.cs:line 365
   at NUnit.VisualStudio.TestAdapter.NUnit3TestExecutor.RunAssembly(String assemblyPath, IGrouping`2 testCases, TestFilter filter) in D:\repos\NUnit\nunit3-vs-adapter\src\NUnitTestAdapter\NUnit3TestExecutor.cs:line 275
```

The culprit appears to be holes in the logic added with https://github.com/nunit/nunit3-vs-adapter/pull/1001 cc @OsirisTerje 

Depending on how you look at https://github.com/nunit/nunit3-vs-adapter/pull/1001 introduced a handful of quirks / bugs.

1) `<WorkDirectory>` is now required when using `TestOutputXml` and *not* using `OutputXmlFolderMode`.  Otherwise NUnit will crash with the first set of exceptions.

2) Using `TestOutputXml` with an absolute path and `<OutputXmlFolderMode>AsSpecified</OutputXmlFolderMode>` is broken.  The dependeny on `WorkDirectory` is avoided thanks to https://github.com/nunit/nunit3-vs-adapter/blob/d0f38dcabd1723071590d4d4296c9bc38703eb77/src/NUnitTestAdapter/AdapterSettings.cs#L436 however, that means `TestOutputFolder` is not uninitialized and the logic over in https://github.com/nunit/nunit3-vs-adapter/blob/d0f38dcabd1723071590d4d4296c9bc38703eb77/src/NUnitTestAdapter/NUnit3TestExecutor.cs#L365 cannot handle that.  And you get the second exception.

3) There is a new invalid set of values that leads to an exception.  If I make a mistake and have a relative `TestOutputXml` and use `<OutputXmlFolderMode>AsSpecified</OutputXmlFolderMode>` I get the following exception.  Prior to https://github.com/nunit/nunit3-vs-adapter/pull/1001 this mistake was not possible.

```
The value cannot be an empty string. (Parameter 'path')
   at System.ArgumentException.ThrowNullOrEmptyException(String argument, String paramName)
   at System.IO.Directory.CreateDirectory(String path)
   at NUnit.VisualStudio.TestAdapter.NUnit3TestExecutor.CreateTestOutputFolder() in D:\repos\NUnit\nunit3-vs-adapter\src\NUnitTestAdapter\NUnit3TestExecutor.cs:line 365
   at NUnit.VisualStudio.TestAdapter.NUnit3TestExecutor.RunAssembly(String assemblyPath, IGrouping`2 testCases, TestFilter filter) in D:\repos\NUnit\nunit3-vs-adapter\src\NUnitTestAdapter\NUnit3TestExecutor.cs:line 275
```

Is `OutputXmlFolderMode.AsSpecified` adding value? Would it be simpler to remove this value and add Path.IsRelative checks so that an absolute `TestOutputXml` value will always be respected regardless of the `OutputXmlFolderMode` value?

I was able to find a way around the problems introduced by https://github.com/nunit/nunit3-vs-adapter/pull/1001.  I switched to using
```
<TestOutputXml>results/TestResult_NUnitTest</TestOutputXml>
    <WorkDirectory>C:/UnitySrc/dev/il2cpp-s-1/il2cpp-s-1</WorkDirectory>
```

And that got past the exceptions.  The following also avoids the bugs
```
<TestOutputXml>C:/UnitySrc/dev/il2cpp-s-1/il2cpp-s-1/results/TestResult_NUnitTest</TestOutputXml>
    <WorkDirectory>C:/UnitySrc/dev/il2cpp-s-1/il2cpp-s-1</WorkDirectory>
```

Because `Path.Combine(WorkDirectory, TestOutputXml)` will return `TestOutputXml` if it is already an absolute path

body: @CharliePoole I set this to Off for the engine, and I don't think it would work without that.  Can recheck of course.

You could be right. I often advise users of the console runner to just use the defaults unless they have some need to change them. Generally, for users, that's the best to do because as soon as you start specifying options you can run into problems. 

But when calling the engine programmatically, that may not be the best way.
